questions.question: Which of the following places is related to Gandhi's Satyagraha of the year 1917?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Champaran.

📌 📌 Key Points

Champaran Satyagraha of 1917

It was the first civil disobedience movement in India.

Champaran district is a historic region in Bihar, India, that is now divided into the East Champaran district and the West Champaran district.

Farmers in this region revolted against the British in 1914 and 1916 over the conditions imposed on indigo cultivation.

Earlier, similar conditions existed in Bengal, but as a result of a major uprising in 1859-61, the peasants there won their freedom from the indigo planters.

Champaran is a district in the state of Bihar where tens of thousands of landless serfs, indentured labourers, and poor farmers were forced to grow indigo and other cash crops instead of food crops.

The European planters had forced the peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of the total land area (called the tinkathia system).

When German synthetic dyes replaced indigo at the end of the nineteenth century, European planters demanded high rents and illegal dues from the peasants in order to maximize their profits before the peasants could switch to other crops.

The first Satyagraha movement, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, took place in the Bihar district of Champaran in 1917.

The Champaran Satyagraha was the first to be launched, but the term Satyagraha was first used in the Anti-Rowlatt Act agitation.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Kheda Satyagrah-

1918 was a year of failed crops in the Kheda district of Gujarat due to droughts.

As per law, the farmers were entitled to remission if the produce was less than a quarter of the normal output.

But the government refused any remission from paying land revenue.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, under Gandhi’s guidance, led the farmers in protest against the collection of taxes in the wake of the famine.

The protest was peaceful and people showed remarkable courage even in the face of adversities like confiscation of personal property and arrest.

Finally, the authorities gave in and gave some concessions to the farmers.

Kheda peasant struggle :

The Kheda Satyagraha of 22 march 1918, in the Kheda district of Gujarat.

India during the period of the British Raj, was a Satyagraha movement organized by Mohandas Gandhi.

It was a major revolt in the Indian independence movement.

It was the third Satyagraha movement after Champaran Satyagraha and Ahmedabad mill strike.

Bardoli Satyagraha:

The Bardoli satyagraha took place in Gujarat and was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

It was a tax revolt that took place in 1928 in the taluka (sub-district) of Bardoli, located in the district of Surat in south Gujarat.

Patel had gathered all the Muslims and Hindus in Bardoli and performed non-violent satyagraha in a revolt against the British.

The protest achieved its principal objective, which included forcing the colonial state to withdraw a policy aimed at raising the rate of land revenue paid by peasants.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan primarily focused on the 'Garibi Hatao' initiative?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fifth Five-Year Plan.

📌 📌 Key Points

Fifth Five Year Plan: Its duration was 1974 to 1978. This plan focussed on Garibi Hatao, employment, justice, agricultural production, and defense.

The Electricity Supply Act was amended in 1975, a Twenty-point program was launched in 1975, the Minimum Needs Programme (MNP), and the Indian National Highway System was introduced.

📌 📌 Additional Information

First Five Year Plan: It was launched for the duration of 1951 to 1956, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru. It was based on the Harrod-Domar model with a few modifications. Its main focus was on the agricultural development of the country.

Second Five Year Plan: It was made for the duration of 1956 to 1961, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru. It was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model made in the year 1953. Its main focus was on the industrial development of the country.

Third Five-Year Plan: It was made for the duration of 1961 to 1966, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru. This plan is also called ‘Gadgil Yojna’, after the Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission D.R. Gadgil. The main target of this plan was to make the economy independent. The stress was laid on agriculture and the improvement in the production of wheat.

Plan Holidays: Due to the failure of the previous plan, the government announced three annual plans called Plan Holidays from 1966 to 1969. The main reason behind the plan holidays was the Indo-Pakistani war and the Sino-India war, leading to the failure of the third Five Year Plan.

Fourth Five-Year Plan: Its duration was from 1969 to 1974, under the leadership of Indira Gandhi. There were two main objectives of this plan i.e. growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.

Rolling Plan: After the termination of the fifth Five Year Plan, the Rolling Plan came into effect from 1978 to 1980. In 1980, Congress rejected the Rolling Plan, and a new sixth Five Year Plan was introduced.

Sixth Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 1980 to 1985, under the leadership of Indira Gandhi. The basic objective of this plan was economic liberalization by eradicating poverty and achieving technological self-reliance.

Seventh Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 1985 to 1990, under the leadership of Rajiv Gandhi. The objectives of this plan include the establishment of a self-sufficient economy, opportunities for productive employment, and up-gradation of technology.

Eighth Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 1992 to 1997, under the leadership of P.V. Narasimha Rao. In this plan, the top priority was given to the development of human resources i.e. employment, education, and public health.

Ninth Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 1997 to 2002, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The main focus of this plan was “Growth with Social Justice and Equality”.

Tenth Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 2002 to 2007, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. II. This plan aimed to double the Per Capita Income of India in the next 10 years.

Eleventh Five Year Plan: Its duration was from 2007 to 2012, under the leadership of Manmohan Singh. It was prepared by C. Rangarajan.Its main theme was “rapid and more inclusive growth”. Twelfth Five Year Plan: Its duration is from 2012 to 2017, under the leadership of Manmohan Singh. Its main theme is “Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth”.

questions.question: In which musical note did Newland put the metals Co and Ni with halogens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Do.

📌 📌 Key Points

John Newlands, a British chemist, proposed the Law of Octaves in 1864.

This law stated that when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic mass, every eighth element has properties similar to the first.

He compared this pattern to the octaves of music, where every eighth note is similar to the first.

However, Newlands' Law of Octaves had limitations.

It didn't work for all elements, especially those with higher atomic masses.

To accommodate all the known elements, he had to place two elements in the same slot in some cases.

One such instance was with cobalt (Co) and nickel (Ni), which he placed in the same slot as the halogens.

This placement highlights the limitations of Newland's classification system.

While it was a significant step towards understanding the periodic relationships between elements, it was not entirely accurate and was eventually superseded by more comprehensive periodic tables, such as Mendeleev's Periodic Table.

Akbar’s Coronation at Kalanaur – Key Details

Context:

Humayun died on 24 January 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library (Purana Qila, Delhi).

At that time, Akbar was in Punjab, campaigning with his guardian and regent Bairam Khan against the Afghans.

Place of Coronation:

Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur, a small town in present-day Gurdaspur district, Punjab.

Age & Date:

The Mughals were still not fully secure in India.

Akbar’s early reign (till about 1560) is often called the “regency period under Bairam Khan.”

Why Kalanaur? (Significance):

Kalanaur was chosen because:

The Mughal army was already stationed in Punjab, a frontier and conflict zone.

It was not safe to immediately go to Delhi or Agra after Humayun’s death.

So, Akbar’s empire formally began from Kalanaur, not from Delhi/Agra.

questions.question: The climate of a place is NOT affected by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Type of soil.

📌 📌 Key Points

The first scientific classification of soil was done by Vasily Dokuchaev.

In India, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has classified soils into 8 categories.

They are:

Alluvial Soil

Black Cotton Soil

Red & Yellow Soil

Laterite Soil

Mountainous or Forest Soil

Arid or Desert Soil

Saline and Alkaline Soil

Peaty and Marshy Soil

📌 📌 Additional Information

Alluvial Soil:

Alluvial soils are widespread in the northern plains and river valleys.

It covers about 40% of the total land area of the country.

These soils are mainly derived from the debris brought down from the Himalayas.

In the Peninsular region, they are found in deltas of the east coast and in the river valleys.

The colour of the alluvial soil varies from light grey to ash grey.

Red & Yellow Soil:

Also known as the “omnibus group”.

It covers about 18.5 % of the total land area of the country.

It is found in regions of low rainfall (eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau).

Along the piedmont zone of the Western Ghats, a long stretch of area is occupied by red loamy soil.

This soil is also present in parts of Odisha and Chattisgarh and in the southern parts of the Middle Ganga Plain.

Black or Regur Soil:

Black soil is also known as “Regur Soil” or the “Black Cotton Soil”.

It covers about 15% of the total land area of the country.

It covers most of the Deccan Plateau – parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and some parts of Tamil Nadu. In the upper reaches of the Godavari and Krishna, and the north-western part of Deccan Plateau, the black soil is very deep.

The colour of these soils varies from deep black to grey.

Desert Soil:

Also known as arid soil, it accounts for over 4.42 % of the total land area of the country.

The colour ranges from red to brown.

Desert soils are sandy to gravelly in texture, have low moisture content and low water-retaining capacity.

These soils are saline in nature and in certain regions the salt content is so high that common salt is obtained by evaporating water.

Laterite Soil:

The name has been derived from the Latin word “later” which means brick.

It accounts for about 3.7% of the total area of the country.

These are typical soils of the monsoon climate which is characterised by seasonal rainfall.

With rain, lime and silica are leached away, and soil rich in iron oxide and aluminium are left leading to the formation of laterite soil.

Laterite soil is deficient in organic matter, nitrogen, phosphate and calcium, however iron oxide and potash are in abundance.

Mountain Soil:

This type of soil is found in the forest regions where rainfall is sufficient.

The texture of the soil depends on the mountain environment where they are found.

These soils are coarse-grained in the upper slopes and loamy and silty on valley sides.

Peaty and Marshy Soils:

These soils are found in regions of heavy rainfall and high humidity, and it supports the good growth of vegetation.

Peaty soils are rich in humus and organic matter.

These soils are generally heavy and black in colour.

In many places, these soils are alkaline.

These are found in southern Uttarakhand, the northern part of Bihar, and the coastal areas of West Bengal, Odisha and Tamil Nadu.

Saline and Alkaline Soils:

These soils have high percentages of sodium, magnesium and potassium, and hence are infertile.

The high salt content is mainly because of the dry climate and poor drainage.

The texture ranges from sandy to loamy.

These soils are found in arid and semi-arid areas, and in waterlogged and swampy regions.

These soils are deficient in calcium and nitrogen.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct with regards to the history of calculating National Income (NI) in India?

📌 📌 Additional Information

Dadabhai Naoroji

Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the Grand Old Man of India, was a leading figure in the early Indian independence movement and a founder of the Indian National Congress.

His activities were mainly in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

The Indian Independence League, however, was primarily active during the 1940s, significantly after Naoroji's most impactful years and following his death in 1917.

This organization sought to obtain independence for India from British rule during World War II, with notable connections to Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army (INA).

Naoroji founded or was associated with several organizations, like the Bombay Association (the oldest political organization in Bombay), the East India Association (established in London to discuss Indian affairs), and Gyan Prasarak Mandali (for the education of adult men in Bombay).

These affiliations reflected his focus on political advocacy, economic theories (notably the Drain Theory), and social reform both in India and the UK.

The Indian Independence League's context and methods, focused on leveraging the geopolitical situations during World War II for India's independence through more direct action, were distinct and not within Naoroji's lifetime or direct activities.

​PC Mahalanobis

The Second five-year plan was based on the Mahalanobis model, an economic development model developed by the Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.

PC Mahalanobis established the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta in 1931 and for the same reason, he is known as the father of Indian Statistics. He was a member of the first Planning Commission of free India.

The second five-year plan was for the year 1956-1961.

The second five-year plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid Industrialisation. The plan attempted to determine a balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors in order to maximize long-run economic growth.

As a result, hydroelectric power projects across the country and five steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of Russia, Britain (the U.K), and West Germany respectively. Coal production was increased. More railway lines were added all over the country.

The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and Atomic Energy Commission of India was established to promote research in India.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.A: They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.
options.B: These have moral and political sanctions.
options.C: They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
options.D: They are positive, as they require the State to do certain things.

questions.correct_answer: They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.

📌 📌 Key Points

The Directive Principles of State Policy of India are the guidelines or principles given to the institutes for governing India and are provided in Part IV of the Constitution of India.

Directive Principles of State Policy aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.

They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state. Directive principles are classified under the following categories; economic, socialistic, political, executive, justice and legal, administrative, environmental, protection of monuments, peace, and security.

Hence, it can be said that the Directive Principles of State Policy are fundamental for the Governance of the state.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Features of DPSPs

The phrase ‘Directive Principles of State Policy’ denotes the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.

These are the constitutional instructions or recommendations to the State in legislative, executive, and administrative matters. According to Article 36, the term ‘State’ in Part IV has the same meaning as in Part III dealing with Fundamental Rights.

Therefore, it includes the legislative and executive organs of the central and state governments, all local authorities, and all other public authorities in the country.

The Directive Principles resemble the ‘Instrument of Instructions’ enumerated in the Government of India Act of 1935.

In the words of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, ‘the Directive Principles are like the instrument of instructions, which were issued to the Governor-General and to the Governors of the colonies of India by the British Government under the Government of India Act of 1935. What is called Directive Principles is merely another name for the instrument of instruction. The only difference is that they are instructions to the legislature and the executive’.

The Directive Principles constitute a very comprehensive economic, social and political program for a modern democratic State.

They aim at realizing the high ideals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as outlined in the Preamble to the Constitution.

They embody the concept of a ‘welfare state’ and not that of a ‘police state’, which existed during the colonial era3. In brief, they seek to establish economic and social democracy in the country.

The Directive Principles are non-justiciable in nature, that is, they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.

Therefore, the government (Central, state, and local) cannot be compelled to implement them.

Nevertheless, the Constitution (Article 37) itself says that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

The Directive Principles, though nonjusticiable in nature, help the courts in examining and determining the constitutional validity of a law.

The Supreme Court has ruled many times that in determining the constitutionality of any law if a court finds that the law in question seeks to give effect to a Directive Principle, it may consider such law to be ‘reasonable’ in relation to Article 14 (equality before law) or Article 19 (six freedoms) and thus save such law from unconstitutionality.

Out of the four hybrid orbitals, one contains a lone pair of electrons and the other three are half filled.

Three half-filled sp3 hybrid orbitals of N atom overlap with half-filled 1s orbital of three hydrogen atoms to form three sigma covalent bonds. Thus, in NH3 molecule, there are three bonding pairs of electrons and one lone pair of electrons.

​ [Image: https://www.zigya.com/application/uploads/images/drawing1_56c84c3dd4620.png?t=1455967296661]

This single lone pair distorts the bond angle of H-N-H to107.5°. and therefore due to the lone pair effect, the structure of the NH3 molecule is pyramidal with nitrogen at the tip.

questions.question: The ages of two friends, Ram and Ravi, differ by 7 years. Ram's mother Mayadevi is three times as old as Ram, and Ravi is four times as old as his brother Soham. The ages of Mayadevi and Soham differ by 65 years. Find the age of Mayadevi (in years).
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Let Ram's age be x. So, Mayadevi's age = 3x.

Assuming Ravi's age is x − 7 to obtain an integer value.

Soham's age = (x − 7) ÷ 4.

Given difference: 3x − (x − 7) ÷ 4 = 65 ⇒ 11x + 7 = 260 ⇒ 11x = 253 ⇒ x = 23.

Mayadevi's age = 3 × 23 = 69 years.

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Difference between the ages of Ram and Ravi = 7 years

⇒ Mayadevi's age = 3 × Ram's age

⇒ Ravi's age = 4 × Soham's age

⇒ Difference between the ages of Mayadevi and Soham = 65 years

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_7f9a9d57437f4bc79badd502ce099809.png/1777710999.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Let the age of Ram be x years.

⇒ Age of his mother, Mayadevi = 3x years.

⇒ Since Ram and Ravi differ by 7 years, let's assume Ravi's age is x − 7. (Assuming x + 7 will result in a fractional age).

⇒ Age of Ravi's brother, Soham = (x − 7) ÷ 4.

⇒ The difference between the ages of Mayadevi and Soham is 65 years:

⇒ 3x − [(x − 7) ÷ 4] = 65

⇒ (12x − x + 7) ÷ 4 = 65

⇒ 11x + 7 = 260

⇒ 11x = 253

⇒ x = 23

⇒ Therefore, Ram's age = 23 years.

⇒ Mayadevi's age = 3 × 23 = 69 years.

⇒ (Note: If we take Ravi's age as x + 7, we get 11x − 7 = 260 ⇒ x = 267 ÷ 11, which does not yield an integer value for age.)

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Linear Equations in Age Problems

Most age problems can be modeled using single-variable linear equations by expressing all ages in terms of one common person's age. Choosing the right central character minimizes complex fractional calculations.

Extraneous or Fractional Values

In quantitative aptitude, if solving an age equation yields a non-integer value where a whole number is expected, try alternating the assumed condition (e.g., swapping which person is older in an absolute difference relationship).

Constant Age Difference

The age difference between any two individuals remains constant regardless of the time elapsed, whereas the ratio of their ages changes continuously over the years.

questions.question:
What is the value of D, if A : C = B : D in the given table?

| A | B | C | D |
| 25 | 40 | 30 | ? |
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Given the proportion: A : C = B : D

Substitute the values from the table: 25 : 30 = 40 : D

Simplify the ratio of A to C: 25 / 30 = 5 / 6

Equating the parts: 5 units = 40 → 1 unit = 8

Therefore, D = 6 units = 6 × 8 = 48

∴ The correct answer is 48.

Alternate Method

Given:

Value of A = 25

Value of B = 40

Value of C = 30

Formula Used:

Proportion rule: If four values are in proportion such that A : C = B : D, then A × D = B × C

Calculation:

⇒ A / C = B / D

⇒ 25 / 30 = 40 / D

⇒ 5 / 6 = 40 / D

Cross-multiplying the terms:

⇒ 5 × D = 40 × 6

⇒ 5 × D = 240

⇒ D = 240 ÷ 5

⇒ D = 48

∴ The correct answer is 48.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Proportion Rule

When two ratios are set equal to each other, they form a proportion. In any valid proportion a : b = c : d, the product of the extreme terms equals the product of the mean terms (a × d = b × c).

Fourth Proportional

If four variables a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then d is known as the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. It can be easily calculated using the direct relation d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two distinct quantities a and b is given by √(a × b). It acts as the middle value x in a continuous proportion where a : x = x : b.

questions.question: By applying which of the following criteria can two triangles NOT be proved congruent?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

For two triangles to be exactly identical (congruent), at least one corresponding side length must be equal.

Standard criteria like SSS, SAS, ASA, and AAS all evaluate at least one side length.

The AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle) criterion only compares angles and completely lacks a side measurement.

Thus, AAA only proves that triangles have the same shape (similarity), but not necessarily the same size.

∴ The correct answer is angle-angle-angle.

Alternate Method

Criteria for proving triangle congruency.

Concept Used:

Congruent triangles must have exactly the same size and shape. All corresponding angles and sides must be equal.

Calculations:

⇒ ASA (Angle-Side-Angle): Valid criterion. If two angles and the included side of one triangle equal the corresponding parts of another, they are congruent.

⇒ SSS (Side-Side-Side): Valid criterion. If all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding sides of another, they are congruent.

⇒ SAS (Side-Angle-Side): Valid criterion. If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another, they are congruent.

⇒ AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle): Invalid criterion for congruence. Having all three corresponding angles equal only ensures the triangles are proportional (similar). For instance, an equilateral triangle with side lengths of 2 cm has angles 60°, 60°, 60°, and an equilateral triangle with side lengths of 4 cm also has angles 60°, 60°, 60°. 📌 📌 Additional Information

Congruence vs Similarity

Congruent figures have exactly the same shape and size (ratio of corresponding sides is 1). Similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size (ratio of corresponding sides is constant).

RHS Congruence Criterion

RHS (Right Angle-Hypotenuse-Side) applies only to right-angled triangles. If the hypotenuse and one side of a right triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and corresponding side of another right triangle, they are congruent.

AAS Congruence Criterion

If any two angles and a non-included side of one triangle are exactly equal to the corresponding angles and side of another triangle, the two triangles are geometrically congruent.

questions.question: \(\frac{2+tan^22A+cot^22A}{sec\ 2A \ .\ cosec\ 2A}\) is equal to ___________.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Put 2A = 45° for quick evaluation.

Numerator = 2 + tan2 45° + cot2 45° = 2 + 12 + 12 = 4

Denominator = sec 45° × cosec 45° = √2 × √2 = 2

Expression value = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

Check Option 4: sec 45° × cosec 45° = √2 × √2 = 2 (Matches perfectly)

∴ The correct answer is sec 2A × cosec 2A.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = (2 + tan2 2A + cot2 2A) ÷ (sec 2A × cosec 2A)

Formula Used:

1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ

1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ

sec2 θ + cosec2 θ = sec2 θ × cosec2 θ

Calculation:

⇒ Split 2 into 1 + 1 to use standard trigonometric identities.

⇒ Numerator = (1 + tan2 2A) + (1 + cot2 2A)

⇒ Numerator = sec2 2A + cosec2 2A

⇒ Using the standard identity: sec2 2A + cosec2 2A = sec2 2A × cosec2 2A

⇒ Substitute this back into the given expression.

⇒ Expression = (sec2 2A × cosec2 2A) ÷ (sec 2A × cosec 2A)

⇒ Cancel out the common terms from numerator and denominator.

⇒ Expression = sec 2A × cosec 2A

∴ The correct answer is sec 2A × cosec 2A.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Sum to Product Conversion Identity

A very useful direct result in trigonometry is sec2θ + cosec2θ = sec2θ × cosec2θ.

Double Angle Formulas

Important double angle relations: sin 2θ = 2sinθcosθ and cos 2θ = cos2θ − sin2θ = 1 − 2sin2θ.

questions.question: If, on a marked price, the difference between selling prices with a discount of 65% and with two successive discounts of 30% and 40% is ₹105, then the marked price (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Effective successive discount of 30% and 40% = 30 + 40 − (30 × 40) ÷ 100 = 58%

Difference in discount percentages = 65% − 58% = 7%

Given difference in Selling Prices = ₹105

⇒ 7% of Marked Price = 105

⇒ Marked Price = 105 × (100 ÷ 7) = 1500

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

First discount (D1) = 65%

Second discount series = Two successive discounts of 30% and 40%

Difference in Selling Prices = ₹105

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_6ede442f593e4bec9cfab8dc0637e371.png/1777711824.png]

Formula Used:

Effective discount for two successive discounts A% and B% = A + B − (A × B) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Effective second discount (D2) = 30 + 40 − (30 × 40) ÷ 100

⇒ D2 = 70 − 12 = 58%

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100%.

⇒ Selling Price 1 (SP1) = 100% − 65% = 35% of MP

⇒ Selling Price 2 (SP2) = 100% − 58% = 42% of MP

⇒ Difference in Selling Prices = SP2 − SP1

⇒ Difference in SP = 42% − 35% = 7% of MP

⇒ We are given that the difference is ₹105.

⇒ 7% of MP = ₹105

⇒ 1% of MP = 105 ÷ 7 = ₹15

⇒ 100% of MP (Marked Price) = 15 × 100 = ₹1,500

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,500.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Successive Discounts

When two discounts D1% and D2% are given successively, the effective single discount is calculated as [D1 + D2 − (D1 × D2) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price & Discount Relation

Discount is always computed on the Marked Price (MP). The final Selling Price (SP) is calculated as MP − Discount Amount. Therefore, Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Effective Equivalent Pricing

A single larger discount percentage generally offers more savings to the buyer compared to two successive discounts that add up to the same numerical sum (e.g., 65% is a bigger discount than 30% and 35% successively).

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, sin(θ) = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos(θ) = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan(θ) = Perpendicular / Base.

For standard angles: sin(30°) = 1/2, cos(30°) = √3/2, and tan(30°) = 1/√3.

questions.question: A money bag contains one rupee, 5 rupee and 10 rupee coins in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7 respectively. If the total amount in the bag is ₹980, then find the number of coins of ₹10.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Value ratio of ₹1, ₹5, and ₹10 coins = (1 × 3) : (5 × 5) : (10 × 7) = 3 : 25 : 70

Total value units = 3 + 25 + 70 = 98 units

Since 98 units = ₹980, 1 unit = ₹10

Total value of ₹10 coins = 70 units = ₹700

Number of ₹10 coins = 700 ÷ 10 = 70

∴ The correct answer is 70 coins.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of number of ₹1, ₹5, and ₹10 coins = 3 : 5 : 7

Total amount in the bag = ₹980

Formula Used:

Total Value = Denomination × Number of coins

Calculations:

⇒ Let the number of ₹1, ₹5, and ₹10 coins be 3x, 5x, and 7x respectively.

⇒ Value of ₹1 coins = 1 × 3x = 3x

⇒ Value of ₹5 coins = 5 × 5x = 25x

⇒ Value of ₹10 coins = 10 × 7x = 70x

⇒ Total value = 3x + 25x + 70x = 98x

⇒ 98x = 980

⇒ x = 980 ÷ 98 = 10

⇒ Number of ₹10 coins = 7x = 7 × 10 = 70

∴ The correct answer is 70 coins.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Coins based on Value Ratio

When the total number of coins is given but their value ratio is provided, divide the value ratio by the respective denomination to find the ratio of the number of coins.

Coins based on Number Ratio

When the total value is given and the ratio of the number of coins is provided, multiply the number ratio by the respective denomination to find the value ratio.

Proportional Division

If a total quantity T is to be divided in the ratio a : b : c, the individual parts are given by T × a / (a+b+c), T × b / (a+b+c), and T × c / (a+b+c).

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest 5-digit number divisible by 47?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

The largest 5-digit number is 99999.

Divide 99999 by 47 to find the remainder.

99999 ÷ 47 gives a quotient of 2127 and a remainder of 30.

Subtract the remainder from 99999 to find the exact largest multiple.

Required number = 99999 − 30 = 99969.

∴ The correct answer is 99969.

Alternate Method

Given:

We need to find the largest 5-digit number divisible by 47.

Concept Used:

According to the division algorithm: Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. To make a number perfectly divisible by a divisor without exceeding it, we must subtract the remainder from the dividend.

Calculations:

⇒ The largest 5-digit number is 99999.

⇒ Let us divide 99999 by 47.

⇒ First, 99 ÷ 47 = 2 with a remainder of 5.

⇒ Bringing down 9, we get 59. 59 ÷ 47 = 1 with a remainder of 12.

⇒ Bringing down 9, we get 129. 129 ÷ 47 = 2 with a remainder of 35.

⇒ Bringing down the final 9, we get 359. 359 ÷ 47 = 7 with a remainder of 30.

⇒ The final remainder is 30.

⇒ To make it exactly divisible by 47, we subtract the remainder from 99999.

⇒ Required Number = 99999 − 30

⇒ Required Number = 99969

∴ The correct answer is 99969.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Division Algorithm

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. Subtracting the remainder from the dividend makes the result perfectly divisible by the divisor.

Smallest n-digit number divisible by 'd'

Divide the smallest n-digit number (e.g., 10000 for 5 digits) by the divisor 'd' to find the remainder 'r'. The required smallest divisible number is (Smallest n-digit number) + (d − r).

Nearest number to 'N' divisible by 'd'

Find the remainder 'r' when N is divided by d. If r < d/2, subtract r from N. If r > d/2, add (d − r) to N.

questions.question: If a right circular cone of height 24 cm has a volume of 1232 cm3, then the total surface area of the cone is:
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Volume = (1/3)πr2h = 1232 ⇒ (1/3) × (22/7) × r2 × 24 = 1232

⇒ r2 = (1232 × 7) ÷ 176 = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25), the slant height l = 25 cm.

TSA = πr(r + l) = (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 25) = 22 × 32 = 704 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 704 cm2.

Alternate Method

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_94798f98fc544189a042540cd062fdfd.png/1777642387.png]

Given:

Height of the cone (h) = 24 cm

Volume of the cone (V) = 1232 cm3

Formula Used:

Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr2h

Slant height (l) = √(r2 + h2)

Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(r + l)

Calculations:

⇒ 1232 = (1/3) × (22/7) × r2 × 24

⇒ 1232 = (176/7) × r2

⇒ r2 = (1232 × 7) ÷ 176

⇒ r2 = 49

⇒ Radius (r) = 7 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(72 + 242)

⇒ l = √(49 + 576)

⇒ l = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ TSA = (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 25)

⇒ TSA = 22 × 32 = 704 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 704 cm2.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Curved Surface Area of a Cone

The curved surface area (CSA) covers only the lateral curved side of the cone. Formula: CSA = πrl.

Volume of a Cone

The internal capacity of a cone is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height. Formula: V = (1/3)πr2h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard sets of integers that satisfy a2 + b2 = c2 speed up geometry computations considerably. Common examples: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17).

questions.question: Let 0º < t < 90º. Then which of the followings is true?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

For any angle t < 45º, we can easily verify the relation by substituting a standard value like t = 30º.

From trigonometric tables, we know that sin(30º) = 0.5 and cos(30º) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866.

Comparing both results, it is clearly evident that 0.5 < 0.866.

This confirms that sin(30º) < cos(30º), establishing that sin(t) < cos(t) for all t < 45º.

∴ The correct answer is sin(t) < cos(t) when t < 45º.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ The angle t lies in the first quadrant where 0º < t < 90º

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_1637bdfded12448eb02798d95a20ea2a.png/1777720883.png]

Calculations:

⇒ In the first quadrant (0º to 90º), the sine function is strictly increasing while the cosine function is strictly decreasing.

⇒ At the exact midpoint t = 45º, both functions intersect and are equal: sin(45º) = cos(45º) = 1/√2.

⇒ For the interval 0º < t < 45º, the cosine curve lies above the sine curve. Therefore, sin(t) < cos(t).

⇒ For the interval 45º < t < 90º, the sine curve lies above the cosine curve. Therefore, sin(t) > cos(t).

⇒ Checking all given statements against these intervals, only the condition for t < 45º matches correctly.

∴ The correct answer is sin(t) < cos(t) when t < 45º.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Behavior of Tangent Function

For 0º < t < 90º, tan(t) is strictly increasing from 0 to infinity. At the midpoint t = 45º, tan(45º) = 1.

Complementary Angle Properties

Trigonometric functions of complementary angles are directly related by: sin(90º − t) = cos(t) and cos(90º − t) = sin(t).

Trigonometric Identities

The foundational Pythagorean identity holds true for all possible values of t: sin2(t) + cos2(t) = 1.

questions.question: Ramesh purchased some items from a dealer on 19 November 2019. The bill generated was for ₹5,480. He had also purchased some items on 10 November 2019 having the bill value of ₹9,800. He cleared both the bills this time and paid the total amount in cash. If the dealer gives a scheme of 2% discount on the payments done within 10 days and 5% for the payments made in cash at the time of purchase, then find the amount paid by Ramesh on 19 November 2019.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Bill 1 (10 Nov to 19 Nov = 9 days gap) is eligible for a 2% prompt payment discount.

Bill 2 (purchased and paid on 19 Nov) is eligible for a 5% instant cash discount.

Total Amount = (9800 × 0.98) + (5480 × 0.95)

Total Amount = 9604 + 5206 = 14810

∴ The correct answer is ₹14,810.

Alternate Method

Given:

Bill 1 value = ₹9,800 (Purchased on 10 November 2019)

Bill 2 value = ₹5,480 (Purchased on 19 November 2019)

Payment date for both the bills = 19 November 2019

Discount scheme 1 = 2% for payments cleared within 10 days.

Discount scheme 2 = 5% for payments made in cash at the time of purchase.

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_1852e547b58240a5a4a6045ad937d7a7.png/1777711837.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Time gap for clearing Bill 1 = 19 November − 10 November = 9 days.

⇒ Since Bill 1 is cleared within 10 days, a 2% discount is applicable on it.

⇒ Payable amount for Bill 1 = 9800 × (100 − 2) / 100 = 9800 × 98 / 100 = ₹9,604

⇒ Bill 2 is purchased and paid on the same day in cash, making it eligible for the 5% discount.

⇒ Payable amount for Bill 2 = 5480 × (100 − 5) / 100 = 5480 × 95 / 100 = ₹5,206

⇒ Total amount paid by Ramesh = Payable for Bill 1 + Payable for Bill 2

⇒ Total amount paid = 9604 + 5206 = ₹14,810

∴ The correct answer is ₹14,810.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Cash Discount vs Trade Discount

A trade discount is offered directly on the catalog price to encourage bulk buying, whereas a cash discount is offered on the invoice price to encourage early or prompt payments by the customer.

Effective Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are applied sequentially on a product, the effective overall discount is calculated using the formula: Effective Discount = a + b − (a × b) / 100 %.

Selling Price after Discount

The final selling price of an item after offering a discount of d% on the marked price (MP) is determined by the relation: SP = MP × (100 − d) / 100.

questions.question: Find the gain percentage, given that Priya sold her scooter for ₹42564 gaining \(\frac{1}{6}\)th of the selling price.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Since Gain is 1/6th of the Selling Price (SP), let us assume SP = 6 units.

This means Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP) = ₹42564

Gain = 1/6 of Selling Price

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_013bed684ba0449197de1eac6dd4c3ab.png/1777711821.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 6) × 42564 = ₹7094

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 42564 − 7094 = ₹35470

⇒ Gain % = (7094 ÷ 35470) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Profit & Loss Base Rule

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the question.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price is obtained as: SP = MP − (Discount % × MP ÷ 100).

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a trader sells goods at Cost Price but uses false weights, the profit percentage is given by: [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

A single equivalent discount for two successive discounts of a% and b% is given by the formula: (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: If a + 1/a = 12, then find the value of a² + 1/a².
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

If a + 1/a = k, then a2 + 1/a2 = k2 − 2.

Here, the given value of k = 12.

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 = 122 − 2

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 = 144 − 2 = 142

∴ The correct answer is 142.

Alternate Method

Given:

a + 1/a = 12

Formula Used:

(x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

Calculations:

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (a + 1/a)2 = 122

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 + 2 × a × (1/a) = 144

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 + 2 = 144

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 = 144 − 2

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 = 142

∴ The correct answer is 142.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Formula

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k.

Negative Counterpart Formula

If x − 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 + 2.

Difference of Squares

For finding the difference, use the identity: x2 − 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)(x − 1/x).

questions.question: The side of an equilateral triangle is 28 cm. Taking each vertex as the centre, a circle is described with a radius equal to half the length of the side of the triangle. Find the area of that part of the triangle which is not included in the circles (use π = 22/7).
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

The sum of the three 60° sectors at the vertices of an equilateral triangle forms exactly one semicircle.

Required Area = Area of Equilateral Triangle − Area of Semicircle

Required Area = [(√3 ÷ 4) × side2] − [(1 ÷ 2) × π × radius2]

Required Area = [(√3 ÷ 4) × 282] − [(1 ÷ 2) × (22 ÷ 7) × 142]

Required Area = (196 × 1.73) − 308 = 339.08 − 308 = 31.08 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 31.08 cm2.

Alternate Method

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_fc139d512452428ead80061d6d3439a2.png/1777642345.png]
Given:

Side of the equilateral triangle, a = 28 cm

Radius of the circle, r = a ÷ 2 = 14 cm

Formula Used:

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a2

Area of a sector of angle θ = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2

Calculation:

⇒ Area of the equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × 282

⇒ Area of triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × 784 = 196√3 cm2

⇒ Taking √3 ≈ 1.73, Area = 196 × 1.73 = 339.08 cm2

⇒ The triangle has three identical sectors, each with a central angle of 60°.

⇒ Total area of 3 sectors = 3 × (60° ÷ 360°) × π × 142

⇒ Total sector area = 3 × (1 ÷ 6) × (22 ÷ 7) × 196

⇒ Total sector area = (1 ÷ 2) × 22 × 28 = 11 × 28 = 308 cm2

⇒ Area of the remaining part = Area of triangle − Area of 3 sectors

⇒ Area of the remaining part = 339.08 − 308 = 31.08 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 31.08 cm2.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Properties of Equilateral Triangle

All three sides are equal, and all internal angles are 60°. The height is given by (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Area of a Circular Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ and radius r is given by the formula: A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2.

Incircle and Circumcircle

For an equilateral triangle of side a, the inradius r = a ÷ (2√3) and circumradius R = a ÷ √3. Their area ratio is always 1 : 4.

questions.question: In a circular race of 750 m, X and Y start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 9 km/h and 13.5 km/h, respectively. If they are running in the same direction then, when will they meet again for the first time on the track?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

When running in the same direction, relative speed is the difference between the two speeds.

Relative Speed = 13.5 − 9 = 4.5 km/h

Convert to m/s: 4.5 × (5/18) = 1.25 m/s

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed = 750 ÷ 1.25 = 600 seconds.

∴ The correct answer is 600 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance of the circular track = 750 m

Speed of runner X = 9 km/h

Speed of runner Y = 13.5 km/h

Formula Used:

Time to meet for the first time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_02502e6122b1475884ed282804ce2b39.png/1777718478.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of X in m/s = 9 × (5/18) = 2.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of Y in m/s = 13.5 × (5/18) = 3.75 m/s

⇒ Relative speed (same direction) = Speed of Y − Speed of X

⇒ Relative speed = 3.75 − 2.5 = 1.25 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 750 ÷ 1.25

⇒ Time to meet = 75000 ÷ 125 = 600 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 600 seconds.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Meeting Anywhere on the Track (Same Direction)

Time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S1 − S2).

Meeting Anywhere on the Track (Opposite Direction)

Time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S1 + S2).

Meeting at the Starting Point

To find when runners will meet exactly at the starting point, calculate the time taken by each to complete one round, then take their LCM: LCM(T1, T2).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of speeds is a:b (in lowest terms), the number of distinct meeting points is |a − b| for same direction, and a + b for opposite direction.

questions.question: A bus travels (1)/(3) of the distance initially at a speed of 40 km/h, the next (1)/(3) of the distance 50 km/h, and the final (1)/(3) of the distance at 60 km/h. Find the average speed of the bus for the entire journey. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Let each 1/3 segment of the journey be the LCM of the given speeds (40, 50, and 60) = 600 km.

Total distance of the journey = 3 × 600 = 1800 km.

Total time taken = (600 ÷ 40) + (600 ÷ 50) + (600 ÷ 60) = 15 + 12 + 10 = 37 hours.

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 1800 ÷ 37 ≈ 48.65 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 48.65 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

The speeds for three equal segments of the journey are 40 km/h, 50 km/h, and 60 km/h.

Formula Used:

When a journey is divided into three equal parts with speeds x, y, and z, the formula for average speed is:

Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx)

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_d76265f370e44a5fa73db70557e9362f.png/1777718466.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Let x = 40, y = 50, and z = 60

⇒ Average Speed = (3 × 40 × 50 × 60) ÷ (40 × 50 + 50 × 60 + 60 × 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 360000 ÷ (2000 + 3000 + 2400)

⇒ Average Speed = 360000 ÷ 7400

⇒ Average Speed = 1800 ÷ 37

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 48.648 km/h

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 48.65 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 48.65 km/h.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Average Speed for 2 Equal Distances

When a body travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed over the entire journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

General Average Speed Concept

When distances are unequal, the average speed is strictly calculated by dividing the Total Distance Travelled by the Total Time Taken.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction at speeds x and y, their relative speed is |x − y|. If they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is (x + y).

questions.question: Three pipes P, Q and R can fill a cistern in 40 minutes, 80 minutes and 120 minutes, respectively. Initially, all the pipes are opened. After how much time (in minutes) should the pipes Q and R be turned off so that the cistern will be completely filled in just half an hour?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Total capacity of the cistern = LCM(40, 80, 120) = 240 units.

Efficiency of P = 6, Q = 3, and R = 2 units/min.

Since P works for the entire 30 minutes, work done by P = 30 × 6 = 180 units.

Remaining work to be done by Q and R together = 240 − 180 = 60 units.

Time pipes Q and R were open = 60 ÷ (3 + 2) = 12 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by P = 40 minutes

Time taken by Q = 80 minutes

Time taken by R = 120 minutes

Total time to fill the cistern = 30 minutes (half an hour)

| Pipe | Minutes | Total Work | Efficiency |
| P | 40 | 240 | 6 |
| Q | 80 | 3 |
| R | 120 | 2 |

Calculations:

⇒ The cistern is filled in exactly 30 minutes, which means pipe P was kept open for the entire duration of 30 minutes.

⇒ Work done by pipe P alone in 30 minutes = Efficiency × Time = 6 × 30 = 180 units.

⇒ Total work remaining = Total capacity − Work done by P

⇒ Remaining work = 240 − 180 = 60 units.

⇒ This remaining work must have been completed by pipes Q and R before they were turned off.

⇒ Combined efficiency of pipes Q and R = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min.

⇒ Time for which Q and R were kept open = Remaining work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Emptying Pipes (Negative Work)

If a pipe or a leak empties a tank, its efficiency is considered negative. The net filling efficiency becomes (Sum of inlet efficiencies) − (Sum of outlet efficiencies).

Time and Efficiency Relation

Time taken is always inversely proportional to efficiency. The ratio of time taken by two pipes A and B to fill a tank is the exact inverse of their efficiency ratio.

Pipes Working on Alternate Minutes

When pipes operate alternately, calculate the net work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 minutes or 3 minutes). Find out how many such cycles fit into the total work and manually add the remaining efforts for the last fractions.

questions.question: If the sum of three numbers is 18 and the sum of their squares is 36, then find the difference between the sum of their cubes and three times of their product.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Using the direct formula: a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = [(a + b + c) ÷ 2] × [3(a2 + b2 + c2) − (a + b + c)2]

Substitute the given values: Sum = 18, Sum of squares = 36

⇒ Required value = (18 ÷ 2) × [3 × 36 − 182]

⇒ Required value = 9 × [108 − 324] = 9 × (−216) = −1944

∴ The correct answer is −1944.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of three numbers, a + b + c = 18

Sum of their squares, a2 + b2 + c2 = 36

Formula Used:

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c) × [a2 + b2 + c2 − (ab + bc + ca)]

Calculation:

⇒ (18)2 = 36 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 324 − 36 = 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 288 = 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ ab + bc + ca = 144

Now, substitute the values into the second formula:

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 18 × [36 − 144]

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 18 × (−108)

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = −1944

∴ The correct answer is −1944.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Alternative Algebraic Identity

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = [(a + b + c) ÷ 2] × [(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2].

Special Conditional Case

If the sum of the variables a + b + c = 0, then the identity reduces to a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc. This property is frequently tested in competitive exams.

Square of a Trinomial

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca). It helps in finding the sum of the product of variables taken two at a time.

B. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs.

C. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

The paragraph begins by introducing the central concept of literacy and illiteracy in India, setting a contrasting tone regarding the existence of both more literate and illiterate people today: Sentence D.

Sentence A follows, providing a specific example of the paradoxical situation in today's context, more children attending school yet also more children out of school: "More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past."

Sentence B continues by stating that it is not sufficient to blame only the high birth rate for this situation: "But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs."

Sentence C concludes the argument by presenting the idea that illiteracy may actually be the cause of the high birth rate rather than the effect: "Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
